status.en: 6 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 67% fewer than the week before, most of them in Juba, Abiemnom and Warrap.
status.nb: 6 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 67 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Juba, Abiemnom og Warrap.

summary.en: Violence persists in South Sudan with armed groups ambushing civilians, killing two people in Jebel Boma County and five in a road ambush in Warrap County. Security forces seized a truckload of alcohol in Mundri West as part of a substance-abuse crackdown, and a Christian woman was killed after refusing a forced marriage to a Muslim man while two pastors were wounded in a separate attack, prompting women in Greater Mundri to demand protection. The governor of Western Equatoria barred personal bodyguards at SPLM congresses and the governor of Jonglei reported efforts to end clashes in Bor, Duk and Twic East, while elections were postponed again to February 2027. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Vold vedvarer i Sør-Sudan med væpnede grupper som overfaller sivile, drar to personer i Jebel Boma fylke og fem i et veiambulans i Warrap fylke. Sikkerhetsstyrker konfiskerte en lastebil med alkohol i Mundri West som en del av en innsats mot rusmisbruk, og en kristen kvinne ble drept etter å ha nektet et tvangs­ekteskap med en muslimsk mann mens to pastorer ble såret i et separat angrep, noe som fikk kvinner i Greater Mundri til å kreve beskyttelse. Guvernøren i Western Equatoria forbød personlige livvakter på SPLM-kongresser, og guvernøren i Jonglei rapporterte om tiltak for å stoppe sammenstøt i Bor, Duk og Twic East, mens valgene ble utsatt igjen til februar 2027. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
